Team / Novus,

I reviewed the proposed redlines re: withholding and VAT. Summary of recommended approach below: 

- Invoicing: Redwood is willing to invoice Novus AI, Inc. (US parent) for the services if Novus confirms central payment and provides a PO referencing the US entity. This avoids most withholding exposure.
- VAT evidence: If services are consumed by Novus AI Europe Ltd., Redwood will supply VAT invoices and any available VAT registration evidence, but cannot certify tax residency for Novus. We will request customer-supplied VAT registration numbers in the Order Form appendix.
- Gross-up: Redwood prefers NOT to accept open-ended gross-up obligations. If Novus requires protection from withholding, propose a capped gross-up that covers direct withholding taxes up to a defined percentage (e.g., 20%) limited to taxes assessed by the customer's jurisdiction and only where withholding is legally required. Alternatively, a tax credit mechanism: if withholding occurs, Novus provides documentation within 30 days and Redwood issues a credit for the grossed-up amount subject to reconciliation. 

Suggested redline language (high level):
- Customer shall be responsible for all taxes, duties and withholdings, except Redwood's U.S. taxes. If Customer is required by law to withhold taxes from payments to Redwood, Customer shall provide evidence of withholding and remit the net amount. If Customer requests Redwood to gross-up, the parties agree to a capped gross-up not to exceed [X%] or to the tax credit reconciliation process described in Appendix A.

I will add precise language to the redline doc and upload a tracked-change version by EOD. For commercial negotiation: recommend we accept Net 30 + 1% early pay or Net 45 standard; the capped gross-up + credit approach is a reasonable middle ground if Novus insists.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
